current.text: Atlanta has stability in the front office, the coaching staff and the roster. The core is basically the same as last season.
The projected starters are CJ McCollum, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu.
Each of the five starters should play 30 or more minutes.
Lu Dort is the main threat to the minutes of McCollum, Daniels and Alexander-Walker.
Dort is not expected to start over McCollum.
Dort and Daniels will play together some, but they will mostly be staggered for spacing.
Atlanta is a deep team and should use a 10-man rotation.
The expected bench is Dort, Aaron Wiggins, Jock Landale, Kingston Flemings and probably Newell, with Kispert and Dorian Finney-Smith also in the mix.
There is no true point guard. Ball handling is shared among McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels.
Because several starters handle the ball, Dort or Wiggins can replace any of them. Flemings is not an automatic handcuff.
Power forward depth is bad to start the season. A Jalen Johnson injury would turn the rotation upside down.
Center depth took a hit. Henri Veesaar is out for the season and Mouhamed Gueye is injured. Jock Landale is the backup center behind Okongwu.
Quin Snyder wants Okongwu spaced away from the rim when he plays alongside Daniels and Johnson.
McCollum signed an extension.
The McCollum extension delays Kingston Flemings moving into the starting lineup.
The roster is two players over the limit.
Cuts or a small trade are likely before opening day. The candidates are Carter, Nembhard, Hield, Gueye and Kispert.
Atlanta is projected at 46 wins and somewhere between fourth and eighth in the East.
The fantasy playoff schedule is 4-4-3 in weeks 19 to 21. That is 11 games, rank 4 of 30.
Resting players is not a concern, even with 14 back-to-backs. The team did not shut players down late last season.

durable.text: Quin Snyder runs an egalitarian, high-movement offense that wants lots of threes and five-out spacing.
Without a rim anchor, the defense uses more switching and blitzing, which puts the center in different spots.

tags.name: deep rotation
tags.detail: 10-man rotation expected. Dort and Wiggins can cover any guard or wing starter.
tags.new_meaning: The team regularly plays about 10 or more players, so minutes are spread and backups have little handcuff value.

tags.name: shared ball handling
tags.detail: No true point guard. McCollum, Alexander-Walker, Johnson and Daniels share the ball.
tags.new_meaning: The team has no single lead ball handler, so assists and usage are spread across several players.

tags.name: five-out offense
tags.detail: Quin Snyder wants lots of threes and five-out spacing. Okongwu is spaced away from the rim next to Daniels and Johnson.
tags.new_meaning: The coach spaces all five players around the arc, so centers and forwards take more threes than usual.

tags.name: low rest risk
tags.detail: Resting is not a concern. No late-season shutdowns last season.
tags.new_meaning: The team rarely rests or shuts down healthy players, including late in the season.

note: All five Atlanta starters should play 30-plus minutes, and the ball is shared with no true point guard. That keeps McCollum, Alexander-Walker and Daniels useful, and an 11-game, 4-4-3 playoff schedule with no rest worries helps every starter. Watch Lu Dort's minutes against the guards and the roster cuts before opening day. Power forward depth is thin, so a Jalen Johnson injury would reshape the whole rotation.
